The clause covers one situation: a delivery that the carrier has declared lost. It forbids asking the supplier to speed it up.

- **Shipment is lost:** The clause says "a delivery that the carrier has declared lost", which matches a lost shipment, so this one is true.
- **Carrier answers with a status:** A declaration of lost is arguably a carrier status. The clause is about the carrier declaring lost, not about answering with a status in general, so I'm treating this as a narrower case and answering false.
- **All others:** Lateness thresholds, session states, invoices, helper agents, approvals, the supplier language table and a carrier error are not mentioned.

The clause says: if a helper answers after the report is already filed, ignore the answer. Its only trigger is a helper answering late, after the report is filed.

Checking each question against that trigger:
- Shipment lateness (Q1–Q4): not specified.
- Session state (Q5–Q7): not specified.
- Invoice work (Q8–Q10): not specified.
- Q11 asks about a helper agent about to be dispatched. The clause does not cover dispatch, so no.
- Q12 asks about a helper agent dying. The clause does not cover that, so no.
- Q13 asks about a helper named in the routing table. Not covered.
- Approvals (Q14–Q15): not specified.
- Suppliers (Q16–Q17): not specified.
- Carrier answers (Q18–Q19): the clause concerns a helper answering, not a carrier, so no.

The clause says that when the report must edit an invoice (which it never normally does), the agent should read the matching rules just before. The only candidate that matches this trigger is "An invoice file is about to be edited". Every other candidate concerns a different situation, so the rest are false.

Candidate 9 asks about an invoice file about to be edited. The clause says "if it ever must [edit an invoice], read the matching rules the moment before," so this is true.

Candidate 11 asks about an invoice about to be deleted. Deletion is not editing, so this is false.

Candidate 10 asks about a total difference above 50 EUR. The clause says nothing about this, so this is false.

The clause says: a delivery less than one day late stays out of the late table; a delay longer than one day goes in. "Not even one day behind" means under one day. "A longer delay" means longer than one day (more than one day).

Q1: more than two days late. This is a different threshold, so false.
Q2: more than one day late goes in the table. This matches, so true.
Q3: lost shipment. False.
Q4: report has no late shipments. False.
Q5: exactly two days late. This is covered only by the implied "longer delay" rule and is not specified as its own condition. False.

Q6–Q8: session state. False.
Q9–Q11: invoice work. False.
Q12–Q14: helper agent. False.
Q15–Q16: approval. False.
Q17–Q18: supplier. False.
Q19–Q20: carrier. False.

The clause says: if a single invoice line differs by more than 50 EUR, mark that line. It concerns an invoice line difference only.

Checking the candidates:
- Shipment lateness (questions 1–5): not specified.
- Session state (6–8): not specified.
- Work on an invoice: file about to be edited (9) is not specified. Total difference of an invoice above 50 EUR (10) is different, because the clause concerns a single line, not the invoice total. Invoice about to be deleted (11) is not specified.
- Helper agent (12–14): not specified.
- Approval (15–16): not specified.
- Supplier (17–18): not specified.
- Carrier answers (19–20): not specified.

All answers are false.

Only the clause's own trigger counts: a supplier has two languages listed. The questions fall under several topic headings, and I checked each against that trigger.

- **Shipment lateness, session state, invoice work, helper agents and approvals:** none of these match the supplier-language trigger, so all are false.
- **"The supplier of an order":** the questions ask about a supplier being absent from, or present in, the language table. The clause instead covers a supplier with two languages listed, so both are false.
- **Carrier answers:** the clause says nothing about carrier replies, so all are false.
